title: Galvanic Corrosion vs. Electrode Potential
description: Introduction to electrochemical series and corrosion of metals. Explore standard electrode potentials and understand galvanic corrosion when connecting different metals.

components.content:
## Electrochemical Series - Standard Electrode Potentials

This table presents the electrochemical series (electromotive series), which lists metals arranged in order of their standard potentials relative to the hydrogen electrode (SHE).

### Key Principles:

- **Standard Hydrogen Electrode (SHE)**: The reference electrode with a potential of 0.00 volts
- **Standard Electrode Potential**: The potential difference measured between a metal and the SHE
- **Corrosion Rule**: Metals higher up in the series (more negative potentials) displace metals lower in the series. When two metals with different potentials are connected, the metal with the **lowest potential corrodes**.

### Common Corrosion Problem:

When copper and iron/steel are connected in piping systems, iron/steel corrodes **many times faster** than iron/steel alone because iron (-0.44 V) has a lower potential than copper (+0.34 V), making iron the anode that corrodes.

### Potential Difference Calculation:

When two metals are connected, the corrosion rate is influenced by the potential difference between them. The greater the difference, the more aggressive the corrosion.
